correctness.rationale: The four Γ-square hyperedges are all three-corner sets; every nondegenerate Γ-square in a simple graph therefore uses exactly one graph edge. The resulting direct sum of C2 and C1 is compatible with ∂2. The integral normalized cone K_n=(-1)^{n+1}T_n on a single target edge satisfies ∂K+K∂=id-c_u, giving actual edge-supported 3-chain fillers for every graph 2-cycle. Reversal squares give the exact degree-one relation and graph incidence homology. Seven finite graph examples and 232 signed integer cone tests independently check the conventions; this is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The recently introduced Γ cubical homology admits higher-dimensional cubes even for ordinary graphs. The all-graph integral H2 vanishing distinguishes exactly what the first nontrivial higher degree can and cannot detect, and the accompanying natural H1 identification makes a complete low-degree structural comparison. Ordinary graph cubical homology may have nonzero H2, so this is not just ordinary graph theory restated or a mere finite-table calculation. It motivates and bounds future hypergraph computations while making no assertion about dimensions at least three.
